presentation: Help to Buy: depends, up to €35,000. 10% of €380,000 is €38,000, above the €35,000 cap: up to €35,000. The refund is also limited to the Income Tax and DIRT paid over the last four tax years, which was not given. Cap €35,000 for applications from 2026-10-07; homes bought or built by 2029-12-31 (Revenue, checked 2026-11-09).
Central Bank limits: borrowing up to 4 times income (€248,000) and 90% of the price. The highest price they allow is €283,000, or €314,444.44 for a new build with Help to Buy towards the deposit.

At €380,000: a €38,000 deposit is needed, €35,000 of it from Help to Buy; the loan of €310,000 is €62,000 above the income limit, which lenders can exceed for up to 15% of their lending (their decision).
Green rates are the lenders’ own: the lowest at this loan-to-value is AIB 3-year fixed Green A Mortgage, LTV over 80% at 3.2%, against 3.5% standard.
The First Home shared equity scheme could not be confirmed from a primary page, so it is not included.
These are the published rules and the figures for the inputs given; the customer decides.

conditions: A first-time buyer: never bought or built a home before, alone or jointly, in Ireland or abroad.
A new build bought from a builder (construction subject to VAT), a self-build, or a converted non-residential building; not as an investment.
The price (or a self-build’s approved valuation) is €500,000 or less.
The mortgage is at least 70% of the price, from a qualifying lender.
Lived in as the main home for 5 years, or Revenue claws the refund back.
Limited to the Income Tax and DIRT paid over the 4 tax years before applying (USC and PRSI do not count).

sources.fact: New builds (construction subject to VAT), self-builds and converted non-residential buildings; €500,000 or less
The lesser of €35,000 (applications from 7 October 2026), 10% of the price or valuation, and Income Tax and DIRT paid in the four years before applying; USC and PRSI not counted
A first-time buyer, living in it as their main home for five years; a mortgage of at least 70% of the price; bought or built by 31 December 2029

reasons: The refund is also limited to the Income Tax and DIRT paid over the last four tax years, which was not given.

lending.allowance: Each lender may lend above the limits for up to 15% of its first-time-buyer lending, and 15% of its second-and-subsequent-buyer lending, each year. Whether a buyer gets one is the lender’s decision; the figures here do not assume one.
lending.exemptions: Switcher mortgages and arrears restructures are outside both limits; borrowers in negative equity are outside the loan-to-value limit; principal-home bridging loans are outside the income limit (2026).

source.fact: Loan-to-income 4 times (first-time buyers) and 3.5 times (second and subsequent); loan-to-value 90%; allowances 15% of each; framework reviewed October 2022, S.I. 546 of 2022 from 1 January 2023

firstHomeScheme.note: The First Home shared equity scheme (the State takes a share of a new home’s price) could not be confirmed from a primary page on 2026-11-09: whether it is open, its share limits and its local price ceilings are not recorded. See firsthome.ie.

greenRates.note: No Central Bank or government rule sets mortgage rates by BER: lenders set their own green rates. The green rates here are the lenders’ own, from the market data.

ranking.basis: Lowest total cost over 30 years on €310,000: interest at the initial rate for the fixed period and the stated follow-on rate after, less any stated cashback. Rates with no whole-term figure come last.

assumptions: Loan-to-income 4 times gross income; loan-to-value at most 90%. Central Bank of Ireland mortgage measures (https://www.centralbank.ie/financial-system/financial-stability/macro-prudential-policy/mortgage-measures, checked 2026-11-09).

Each lender may lend above the limits for up to 15% of its first-time-buyer lending, and 15% of its second-and-subsequent-buyer lending, each year. Whether a buyer gets one is the lender’s decision; the figures here do not assume one.
Lenders also assess whether the repayments are affordable; these are the regulatory limits only.
The deposit is the savings given; Help to Buy, gifts and other sources count only if included.

Repayments at the initial rate for the fixed period, then the provider’s stated follow-on rate for the rest of the term (it is a “potential” rate and can change). Variable rates are assumed to stay as published.
Cashback is counted where CCPC states a percentage. Fees are listed as the source states them and not added.
Help to Buy is counted towards the deposit, as Revenue pays it to the builder or into the self-build loan.
Rules as recorded on 2026-11-09 from Revenue and the Central Bank; each is listed with its page.
